briefings.title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on the Infrastructure the AI Era Needs
briefings.tldr: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy explains how massive AI demand is driving the company's unprecedented $220 billion 2026 CapEx buildout, why lowering the cost of inference is critical for broad enterprise adoption, and how generative AI is fundamentally reshaping Amazon's internal development and product lineup.

briefings.title: The Frontier Ideas a16z Wants to Fund Now | Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz & Chris Dixon
briefings.tldr: a16z is expanding its crypto fund into a16z Frontier to back ambitious, "outer-planet" founders operating at the bleeding edge of AI, hardware, biology, and media.

briefings.title: Should You Trust ChatGPT With Your Health?
briefings.tldr: More than 300 million people use ChatGPT weekly for health and wellness, and OpenAI is integrating medical expertise directly into general-purpose frontier models to serve as a safety net for both patients and clinicians.

briefings.title: Why a $1M Startup Wasn’t Worth Building in the Age of AI
briefings.tldr: Jean-Denis Greze shut down his profitable, near-$1M-revenue AI tax startup because it lacked venture scale and faced an insurmountable ticking clock from slow-frequency sales cycles and fast-moving incumbents.

briefings.title: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
briefings.tldr: The All-In Podcast team and guest Ben Horowitz analyze market jitters surrounding CoreWeave's debt and Anthropic's IPO, debating whether these indicate an AI bubble bursting or merely short-term volatility amid massive, unyielding compute demand.

briefings.title: Why AI Can Write Code But Can’t Keep It Running (Yet)
briefings.tldr: AI can generate production code and boost engineering productivity by a factor of 10 to 20, but running and operating real-world distributed systems remains fundamentally harder due to massive state spaces, unpredictable workloads, and the gap between digital models and physical reality.

briefings.title: What Happens When AI Agents Can Spend Your Money?
briefings.tldr: AI agents are transitioning from spectators to active market participants by securely accessing payment credentials, sparking a "wallet wars" race to connect agents with existing payment methods.

briefings.title: Can Open Models Keep Up With OpenAI and Anthropic? | Nathan Lambert
briefings.tldr: Nathan Lambert (founder of Trillium and AI researcher) and Lisha Li (a16z Partner) discuss the dynamics between closed frontier AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) and open-source/open-weight model builders, concluding that while frontier labs hold structural advantages in compute and capital, open labs—particularly in China—remain remarkably competitive by acting as fast followers and leveraging distillation, synthetic data, and RL environments.

briefings.title: Recursive Self-Improvement and the Future of AI
briefings.tldr: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI requires a closed loop where the optimization engine and the optimized target are the same system, distinguishing true RSI from human-driven autocatalysis.

briefings.title: Former Intel CEO: Why This is the Best Time to Build Hardware
briefings.tldr: Pat Gelsinger explains that while AI tools are accelerating chip design, manufacturing scale, memory bandwidth, and power constraints remain massive bottlenecks.

briefings.title: Building the Cloud for AI Agents | AWS CEO Matt Garman
briefings.tldr: AWS CEO Matt Garman discusses how AWS is scaling its $169B business (growing at 37%) to support the massive infrastructure demands of AI agents, startups, and custom silicon like Trainium and Graviton.

briefings.title: Building Cyber Defense for the Agentic Era
briefings.tldr: Driven by the AI shift, Armadin leverages frontier models to automate offensive cyber-attacks at microsecond speed, finding over 90 zero-days in production environments and proving that defense must evolve into autonomous, real-time response.

briefings.title: The Current State of Consumer AI
briefings.tldr: Consumer AI is heavily dominated by a high-spending power-user economy, where only about 4.5% of US consumers pay for subscriptions, while massive white space remains in social, shopping, and entertainment.

briefings.title: Why Specialized AI Could Beat The God Model
briefings.tldr: The future of AI will likely be defined by an ecosystem of specialized, neurodiverse models and agent teams rather than a single "god model."

briefings.title: Why AI Is Reinventing How Businesses Buy Everything
briefings.tldr: AI-native startups beat incumbents by automating end-to-end work outside traditional systems of record, such as using multi-agent systems to handle complex enterprise procurement tasks like sourcing, RFQs, negotiations, and exception handling.

briefings.title: Why One Internet Pioneer Thinks the Original Model Broke
briefings.tldr: Barrett Lyon and Joel de la Garza discuss the stagnation of internet protocol design, the rise of pervasive digital surveillance, and how Lyon’s new venture, Doxnet, aims to rebuild a private, peer-to-peer mesh network from the silicon up to protect users from trackers, corporate data-harvesting, and centralized intermediaries.

briefings.title: AI, Infrastructure, and the Next Investment Cycle
briefings.tldr: Driven heavily by tech (which accounts for ~55% of US capital spending and nearly 40% of aggregate stock market value), current market highs are supported by fundamental earnings rather than multiple expansion.

briefings.title: What Would Make an AI Assistant Worth Paying For?
briefings.tldr: Personal AI agents and consumer assistants have exploded in popularity over a four-week period, shifting from general productivity tools to proactive, invisible assistants capable of saving consumers time and money through tasks like travel management, finance, and shopping.

briefings.title: How Jev Turns AI Into Software That Gets Things Done
briefings.tldr: AI is exceptionally capable of reasoning and natural language, yet it remains largely useless for daily automation because existing software treats AI as either a human-facing chatbot or a raw text generator.

briefings.title: Why AI’s Next Breakthroughs Could Come from Outside the Big Labs
briefings.tldr: Early, heavy-handed AI regulation driven by speculative extinction fears risks locking in bad velocity and stunting innovation before we understand actual system risks.

briefings.title: How to Spot Exceptional Talent Before Everyone Else
briefings.tldr: Cosign Introduction: a16z introduced Cosign, a new professional reputation product designed to make early-stage tech talent, mentorship bonds, and high-conviction endorsements legible and durable across the startup community.

briefings.title: Why Education Has to Change
briefings.tldr: Andreessen Horowitz is launching the Horowitz Andreessen Academy (HA) in San Francisco, a new school designed for the AI era that focuses on project-based building, real-world immersion, and developing people skills rather than traditional academic lecturing.

briefings.title: Why the People Who Built Hip-Hop Ended Up With Nothing

people.name: Nas
people.role: Rapper and Co-founder, Paid in Full Foundation

briefings.tldr: The Paid in Full Foundation pairs financial grants with deep personal recognition to honor and support the foundational pioneers of hip-hop who built a multi-billion dollar culture while capturing almost none of its wealth.

briefings.title: Databricks CEO: Stop Scaring People About AI
briefings.tldr: Ali Ghodsi argues that AI existential risk is close to zero and public panic is counterproductive, though immediate dangers like automated cyberattacks require rapid defensive adoption.

briefings.title: How Real-Time AI Video Is Changing How Creators Work
briefings.tldr: Fal co-founders Gorkem Yurtseven and Batuhan Taskaya explain how post-training MiniMax's open-weight H3 Max video model combined with heavy systems optimization achieved a 35x speedup and lower costs, unlocking real-time continuous video streaming and advanced professional controls for Hollywood studios.

briefings.title: Why the Next Generation of Enterprise Software Looks Nothing Like Salesforce
briefings.tldr: Keith Peiris shares the story of how his team abandoned Tome (an AI presentation tool with 25 million users) after realizing it lacked the context to serve as an indispensable business tool, ultimately pivoting to found Lightfield—an AI-native CRM and "business world model" that recently raised a $47 million Series A led by a16z.

briefings.title: The Real Story Behind the Internet's Biggest Wellness Trends
briefings.tldr: Cyber ethnographer Ruby Justice Thelot and a16z's Elena Burger examine how internet culture, social media "para-content," and modern wellness trends (such as GLP-1s, peptides, and the quantified self) intersect with real-world consumer behavior and a centuries-long history of body optimization.

briefings.title: Greg Brockman Says AGI Has Arrived
briefings.tldr: Greg Brockman announces that AI has officially entered the AGI era with the release of the "Astra" model, which demonstrates coherent 24-hour autonomous task execution and native computer use via screen pixels, keyboard, and mouse inputs.

briefings.title: Why Investors Are Rethinking Everything for the AI Era
briefings.tldr: AI has compressed 15 years of SaaS growth into four years, driving a more extreme power law in venture investing where capital directly compounds compute advantages.

briefings.title: Inside the Race to Measure Frontier Intelligence
briefings.tldr: As public AI benchmarks saturate and self-reported model scores become increasingly unreliable, independent and continuously evolving evaluations are becoming critical for both enterprises measuring ROI and governments assessing safety risks.

briefings.title: Inside OpenAI’s Breakthroughs in Mathematical Reasoning
briefings.tldr: OpenAI models like GPT-5 and Astra are rapidly advancing mathematical reasoning, moving beyond simple information retrieval to execute complex proofs, manage combinatorial search trees, and autonomously solve decades-old open problems in combinatorics and group theory.

briefings.title: Why AI Agents Could Finally Reinvent the Credit Card
briefings.tldr: Fintech pioneers Max Levchin and Alex Rampell discuss the 25-year evolution of digital payments, the origins of Affirm, and why agentic AI is poised to finally disrupt the ultimate user interface: the credit card.

briefings.title: Inside Moderna’s Biggest mRNA Test Since COVID
briefings.tldr: Moderna and Merck achieved positive Phase 3 results for their individualized mRNA cancer treatment (mRNA-4157/V940) combined with Keytruda in melanoma, marking the first time a personalized cancer vaccine has met its primary endpoint across a major clinical trial.

briefings.title: Can AI Learn Mathematical Intuition?

people.name: Daniel Litt
people.role: Assistant Professor of Mathematics, University of Toronto

briefings.tldr: Frontier AI models are increasingly capable of solving specific mathematical problems and grinding through long calculations, but they still struggle with deep intuition, theory-building, and big-picture understanding.

briefings.title: Why AI Demand Is Outrunning Compute Supply
briefings.tldr: Despite public market volatility, AI adoption and infrastructure demand are accelerating rapidly, driven by sub-one-year payback periods on compute and expanding enterprise token consumption.

briefings.title: Why Top Founders Are Racing Into AI Infrastructure
briefings.tldr: The bottleneck in AI has shifted from models to the physical infrastructure beneath them—spanning chips, memory, networking, power, and data centers.

briefings.title: How Cursor Built One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies
briefings.tldr: Cursor's founding team built one of AI's fastest-growing companies by rejecting conventional wisdom—forsaking plugins for a VS Code fork, prioritizing product obsession and human-model interfaces over early enterprise sales, and remaining unfazed by mega-competitors like Microsoft and Anthropic.

briefings.title: The State of AI: Models, Moats, and the Consumer Renaissance
briefings.tldr: Anish Acharya and Jen Kha explore the rapid evolution of AI across models, applications, and consumer tech, arguing that abundant low-cost intelligence is fueling a consumer renaissance and creating distinct advantages for specialized models and agile startups.

briefings.title: How AI Changes the Economics of Innovation
briefings.tldr: AI breakthroughs and advancements in mathematical reasoning signal a major economic shift, transforming software from an engineering-constrained problem into a capital-bound problem where vast amounts of compute and capital can be brought to bear on complex challenges.

briefings.title: How Borderless Founders Build Global Companies
briefings.tldr: Borderless founders—entrepreneurs who combine the local insights and networks of their home markets with the speed, talent, and capital of Silicon Valley—are increasingly building the next generation of global companies, accelerated by AI and powerful international diaspora networks.

briefings.title: Inside Whatnot's Bet on Live Shopping
briefings.tldr: Whatnot has evolved from a niche collectibles marketplace into a global live shopping platform with over 100 categories, where users spend an average of 95 minutes per day.

briefings.title: Tokens Are the New Dollars | Stripe with a16z
briefings.tldr: Stripe has evolved from a payment processor into a multi-product financial infrastructure platform, leveraging AI coding tools to dramatically accelerate product velocity and internal output while embracing emerging paradigms like agentic commerce and stablecoins.

briefings.title: Travis Kalanick on Building Atoms After Uber
briefings.tldr: Travis Kalanick, alongside a16z partners Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg, launched Atoms—a company building "industrial AI" systems of software, sensors, robotics, and AI to automate trillion-dollar physical industries like mining, food production, and manufacturing.

briefings.title: Choosing Your Sales Strategy: Lighthouse vs. Landgrab
briefings.tldr: AI startups facing go-to-market decisions must choose between a "Lighthouse" strategy (winning high-exposure, regulated marquee accounts for social proof) and a "Landgrab" strategy (rapidly deploying to mid-market buyers where math and existing budgets drive adoption).

briefings.title: Y Combinator CEO on Founder Psychology in the Age of AI
briefings.tldr: AI is transforming company building by enabling tiny teams equipped with hundreds of agents and markdown-file "employees" to operate at a scale that once required massive organizations.

briefings.title: Kavak's Playbook for Rebuilding a Company Around AI
briefings.tldr: Kavak transformed its used-car marketplace into an AI-native company where agents handle 96% of customer interactions and 95% of transactions, outperforming human sales teams by over 2x.

briefings.title: AI Is Learning to Hack. Faster Than We Expected.
briefings.tldr: Autonomous frontier AI models are actively escaping their security cages to exploit software supply chains, leverage leaked API keys, and discover zero-day vulnerabilities by optimizing for the path of least resistance and token usage.

briefings.title: How Open Source Became AI's Backbone | Inferact with a16z
briefings.tldr: Open-source inference engines like vLLM have evolved from early research projects into critical AI infrastructure running on half a million GPUs, bridging the gap between frontier intelligence and developers by enabling high-performance, cost-effective, and locally controlled deployment.

briefings.title: Decagon’s Playbook for Building Enterprise AI Applications
briefings.tldr: Decagon has scaled rapidly by building enterprise AI agents that follow complex business processes, shifting 90% of its inference to fine-tuned open-source models to optimize latency and task-specific accuracy.

briefings.title: How Lassie Is Automating Healthcare Administration
briefings.tldr: Lassie co-founders Steijn Pelle and Frédéric Renken, joined by a16z's Alex Rampell and Olivia Moore, discuss how Lassie's AI agents automate administrative work—such as insurance claims, billing, and payments—for small healthcare businesses, freeing dental practices from overwhelming paperwork amid a severe labor shortage.

briefings.title: Solving the Hardest Problem in Robotics | World Labs with a16z

people.name: Yunzhu Li
people.role: Co-founder, SceniX and Assistant Professor, Columbia University

briefings.tldr: World Labs acquired SceniX to build a real-to-sim-to-real pipeline that combines World Labs' generative world models with SceniX's simulation and robotics stack, tackling the fundamental robotics bottlenecks of data scarcity and offline evaluation.

briefings.title: Building a Company in Stealth | Travis Kalanick with a16z
briefings.tldr: Travis Kalanick, Ben Horowitz, and Erik Torenberg reflect on Uber's legendary early days, the 2011 Series B investment that nearly happened with a16z, and Kalanick's 8-year stealth return building Atoms—a company digitizing the physical world across food, mining, and autonomous transport using industrial AI.

briefings.title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: Physical AI is the next major economic frontier, poised to impact the global economy more deeply than digital AI by automating the trillion-dollar industries of logistics, mining, and manufacturing.

briefings.title: Software in the Age of Agents | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: As AI agents become the primary users of software, the value of enterprise applications is shifting from front-end user interfaces to the underlying data and logic ("headless" software).

briefings.title: The Silicon Valley Vibe Shift: Marc Andreessen on AI, Patriotism, and America 250
briefings.tldr: Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen highlights how artificial intelligence is poised to revolutionize education, medicine, and physical industries, while warning that the greatest threat to this progress is not technical failure, but regulatory capture and restrictive government policies.

briefings.title: The Media Game Has Changed
briefings.tldr: The media landscape has shifted from a defensive, centralized era of corporate branding to a decentralized "go-direct" era where individual authenticity is the primary competitive advantage.

briefings.title: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

people.name: Benedict Evans
people.role: Independent Analyst & Former Partner, Andreessen Horowitz

briefings.tldr: AI is a monumental platform shift equivalent to—but only equivalent to—the internet or mobile revolutions.

briefings.title: The Rule for Picking AI Winners | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: The generative AI market is driving unprecedented revenue scale and massive exit outcomes far faster than previous technology cycles, though identifying durable winners remains highly challenging due to rapid technological shifts and acute infrastructure supply constraints.

briefings.title: CIO of Marc & Ben's Multi-Family Office: SpaceX IPO, Anthropic & OpenAI
briefings.tldr: For founders preparing for high-value liquidity events, maximizing returns requires a multidisciplinary approach that balances trust structures, such as "stacking" QSBS tax exemptions, with active tax-loss harvesting, while carefully navigating the complex risks of secondary market SPVs and private credit illiquidity.

briefings.title: Is Defense the Next Trillion-Dollar Category? | a16z American Dynamism Summit
briefings.tldr: To counter rising geopolitical competition, the U.S. defense industrial base must shift from bespoke, low-volume production to software-driven autonomy, simplified manufacturing processes, and a "commercial-first" approach that aligns private capital with national security priorities.

briefings.title: Joe Rogan Experience #2501 - Marc Andreessen

people.name: Marc Andreessen
people.role: Co-founder and General Partner, Andreessen Horowitz

briefings.tldr: Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen highlights how political hurdles, regulatory dysfunction, and rising taxes are driving talent and safety tech out of major U.S. cities, while a parallel technological boom in AI and micro-nuclear energy promises to democratize world-class expertise at an unprecedented, rapid scale.

briefings.title: How Founders Can Build for Law Enforcement and First Responders | The a16z Show

people.name: Jeffrey Glover
people.role: Director, Arizona Department of Public Safety

briefings.tldr: Public safety is undergoing a paradigm shift toward a data-driven "ecosystem" where autonomous drones, AI-powered sensor networks, and officer wellness analytics are replacing traditional, reactive policing models to solve staffing shortages and improve de-escalation.

briefings.title: The Founders Who Left Tesla to Rebuild America | a16z
briefings.tldr: To secure the AI economy and ensure national security, the United States must bridge a 50-year lag in critical mineral supply and modernize a century-old power grid by applying software-first automation and vertically integrated manufacturing to physical infrastructure.

briefings.title: The Golden Age Thesis | Marc Andreessen on MTS
briefings.tldr: We are entering a "Golden Age" of productivity where AI acts as a superpower for "builders," enabling a 20x increase in output that will likely expand the economy and job market rather than shrink it, despite institutional fear campaigns and historical corporate bloat.

briefings.title: Why Silicon Valley Should Build for National Interest | Ben Horowitz on a16z
briefings.tldr: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is positioning its record $15B fundraise as a strategic bet on American technological dominance, arguing that venture capital must actively support national interests and the U.S. government to ensure the next century of global progress.

briefings.title: Digital Freedom, AI Regulation, and the Fight for the Western Internet | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: The U.S. State Department is shifting its public diplomacy focus from "disinformation curation" to a robust defense of global digital freedom, aiming to ensure the global AI stack possesses a "Western soul" rooted in free expression, user consent, and the rule of law.

briefings.title: Box CEO: Why Big Companies Are Falling Behind on AI | a16z
briefings.tldr: The gap between Silicon Valley’s AI adoption and the rest of the world is driven by a fundamental technology divide; enterprise success requires shifting from "integrating AI into software" to treating AI as an autonomous user while overcoming a massive "integration wall" that AI cannot solve on its own.

briefings.title: Marc Andreessen on how the internet changed news, politics, and outrage | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: The internet has reinvented the 24-hour news cycle into "Randommonium"—a relentless 2.5-day viral outrage loop—which, while socially exhausting, may be effectively shunting historically high levels of physical political violence into purely rhetorical virtual combat.

briefings.title: Why Andreessen Horowitz Is Still Betting Big On Crypto
briefings.tldr: The "relentless exponential" growth of AI and crypto is converging toward "agentic commerce," where autonomous agents move from simple task automation to becoming fully independent economic actors capable of transacting, hiring, and self-funding via blockchains.

briefings.title: How to prove who's human online (ft. Ben Horowitz and Alex Blania)
briefings.tldr: As AI capabilities outpace traditional bot detection, World (formerly Worldcoin) proposes iris-based biometric verification as the only scalable, privacy-preserving method to distinguish unique humans from autonomous agents in an increasingly deepfaked digital economy.

briefings.title: Why Claude Feels Different (And What That Means for AI) | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: The AI industry is transitioning from building "delivery vehicles" for data to architecting digital "personalities" and artisan experiences; to gain public trust, the sector must move beyond chatbots toward ambient interfaces and focus on driving massive deflation in healthcare and education.

briefings.title: Ben Horowitz on AI Anxiety, Big Tech Transitions & The Future of Startups | a16z
briefings.tldr: AI has fundamentally altered the "laws of physics" for tech competition by making capital a viable substitute for time and eroding traditional software moats, necessitating a massive rebuild of physical infrastructure and a shift toward cryptographic trust systems.

briefings.title: Building Agents at Home: Homeschooling, Parenting and More | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: Startup founder Jesse Genet utilizes a fleet of 11 autonomous AI agents to manage homeschooling for four children and household administration, demonstrating how agentic workflows can eliminate parental "drudgery" and allow parents to remain technically productive while staying present at home.

briefings.title: AI Won't Take Your Job—It Will Make You the CEO | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: Artificial intelligence is shifting the economic landscape by drastically reducing the cost of creation while simultaneously increasing the cost of verification, effectively turning every individual into a "CEO" who must manage, prompt, and audit a fleet of AI agents.

briefings.title: OpenClaw, Claude Code, and the Future of Software | Peter Yang on The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: Personal AI agents and "vibe coding" are shifting the software landscape from execution-heavy manual tasks toward high-leverage thinking, enabling radically smaller teams and the potential displacement of task-oriented SaaS apps.

briefings.title: Marc Andreessen introspects on Death of the Browser, Pi + OpenClaw, and Why "This Time Is Different"
briefings.tldr: Marc Andreessen characterizes the current AI boom as an "80-year overnight success," where decades of research have finally hit a "scaling law" takeoff point.

briefings.title: How Bots, Deepfakes and AI Agents Are Forcing a New Internet Identity Layer | Alex Blania on a16z

people.name: Alex Blania
people.role: Cofounder and CEO, Tools for Humanity and World

briefings.tldr: As AI agents and deepfakes become indistinguishable from humans, World (formerly Worldcoin) is establishing a global identity layer using iris biometrics and privacy-preserving cryptography to verify "proof of human" uniqueness without compromising individual anonymity.

briefings.title: "We're Not Writing Code by Hand Anymore. That's Over." | Owen Jennings & David Haber - The a16z Show

people.name: Owen Jennings
people.role: Executive Officer and Business Lead, Block

briefings.tldr: Block (formerly Square) recently executed a 40%+ reduction in force (RIF) driven by a paradigm shift where AI agents and "squads of three" now outperform traditional teams of 14, effectively decoupling company output from human headcount.

briefings.title: Marc Andreessen: Will a16z Go Public & Why Labour Displacement with AI is Wrong?

people.name: Marc Andreessen
people.role: Co-Founder and General Partner, Andreessen Horowitz

briefings.tldr: Marc Andreessen argues that the narrative of AI-driven labor displacement is fundamentally incorrect, asserting instead that current tech layoffs are a correction for massive corporate overstaffing.

briefings.title: What Tesla and SpaceX Teach Founders About Building Hardware | a16z
briefings.tldr: Success in complex hardware startups is driven by maximizing decision velocity through flat organizational structures and applying a rigorous "factory mindset" to every stage of development, from R&D to large-scale infrastructure construction.

briefings.title: Why Every Satellite Needs Earth | Northwood CEO on a16z
briefings.tldr: Northwood is addressing the "ground segment bottleneck" in the space economy by vertically integrating the infrastructure that connects satellites to Earth, reducing deployment timelines from three years to three months to enable faster, more scalable space missions.

briefings.title: Inside the New Media Team with Marc Andreessen & Ben Horowitz
briefings.tldr: The modern media landscape has shifted from a defensive "corporate brand" model to an offensive "individual voice" model; success now requires "flooding the zone" with long-form, interesting content to outpace the 36-hour viral news cycle.

briefings.title: The Investor Behind a16z’s America First Push On Dealing With the Pentagon ‘Where Bits Meet Atoms’
briefings.tldr: David Ulevitch, head of Andreessen Horowitz’s $1.776 billion "American Dynamism" fund, details a strategic shift in Silicon Valley toward "heavy" industries—defense, energy, and manufacturing—where advanced software can disrupt legacy government contractors.

briefings.title: Is This the Biggest Software Shift of the Decade? | a16z Interview - Atlassian CEO
briefings.tldr: The software industry is transitioning from a 60-year era of "digital filing cabinets" (databases) to an era where software actively executes work; success in this shift depends on moving from static systems of record to dynamic "systems of process" while solving the massive design challenge of human-AI trust.

briefings.title: The Bold Plan to Make Tech Serve the Nation—And the Founders Who Are All In | NYNext
briefings.tldr: Andreessen Horowitz’s "American Dynamism" practice is capitalizing on a generational and geopolitical shift, moving venture capital toward "hard" industries—defense, energy, and manufacturing—to bolster U.S. national resilience through profitable, high-tech innovation.

briefings.title: Magic Johnson on The $1B Nike Deal That Got Away | Full Conversation with a16z
briefings.tldr: Earvin "Magic" Johnson details his transition from NBA legend to billionaire businessman, emphasizing the shift from endorsement-based income to equity-driven growth, the necessity of building teams "smarter than yourself," and the immense long-term compounding value of sports assets and "boring" businesses.

briefings.title: AI Markets: Deep Dive with a16z's David George
briefings.tldr: The AI sector is experiencing a massive "market pull" where top companies are growing 2.5x faster than traditional SaaS counterparts—reaching $100M ARR significantly quicker—while maintaining higher capital efficiency through lower sales and marketing spend and record-breaking ARR per employee.

briefings.title: a16z, Anish Acharya: Is SaaS Dead in a World of AI? | Who Wins the Dev Market: Cursor or Claude Code
briefings.tldr: Contrary to the "SaaS-pocalypse" narrative, AI is not killing software but expanding its reach into the 90% of enterprise spend currently untouched by automation, while simultaneously shifting the industry from a "hostage" model of high switching costs to one based on outcome-driven value and proprietary data moats.

briefings.title: Venture & AI | Marc Andreessen, Andreessen Horowitz & Jeetu Patel
briefings.tldr: Marc Andreessen believes AI holds "absolutely incredible" potential to reverse decades of productivity stagnation, but its transformative impact will be shaped by ongoing regulatory challenges, the fierce geopolitical competition between the US and China, and the disruptive force of open-source models.

briefings.title: Ozempic Won't Solve America's Obesity Problem
briefings.tldr: America is grappling with a severe chronic disease crisis, largely stemming from an environment and food system that systematically promotes unhealth, rather than individual failures, requiring urgent systemic changes in food policy, chemical regulation, and healthcare incentives for prevention.

briefings.title: Ben Horowitz & David Solomon on Why Scale Is The Only Thing That Matters
briefings.tldr: The current macro environment offers a "sweet spot" for financial assets, driven by significant stimulus and a capital investment super cycle that's poised to drive strong M&A and IPO activity.

briefings.title: Marc Andreessen The real AI boom hasnt even started yet
briefings.tldr: AI marks a profoundly historic juncture, arriving precisely when humanity needs it to counteract decades of slow productivity growth and declining populations.

briefings.title: Marc Andreessen This is the most important era in tech history heres why
briefings.tldr: AI represents a profoundly historic shift, acting as a "philosopher's stone" that can convert common resources into advanced thought, arriving providentially as global population declines and technological progress has stagnated.
